headline: FDA rejects Capricor's cell therapy for Duchenne
pages: The Food and Drug Administration said Friday it rejected deramiocel, a cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy developed by Capricor Therapeutics, STAT reports. The treatment was aimed at teenagers and young men with Duchenne who have already lost the ability to walk and have few options. STAT columnist Adam Feuerstein writes that the decision should have been an easy one, because Capricor's two randomized trials both failed to show the therapy could prevent heart failure or preserve arm muscle function. He notes that regulating Duchenne drugs has rarely been straightforward. Source: STAT
